_meta.source: Hand-authored dummy scenario for the Week 4 progress demo -- not a gold-standard-backed evaluation scenario (no gold_standard_threats.json). Deliberately mirrors the genomic scenario's structural pattern (internal staff typed as ExternalEntity, one genuinely external party) at a small, presentable scale.
_meta.purpose: Designed to demonstrate two Week 4 changes live: (1) the internal_staff role/effective_type reclassification recovering otherwise-unreachable flows, and (2) grounded citations against the newly-added HIPAA/GINA/Common Rule regulations.
_meta.demo_notes: DF3 (Nurse->EHR Database), DF4 (Attending Physician->Patient), and DF5 (Genetic Testing Lab Courier->Genetic Test Results Store) are EE-involved interactions only reachable because Nurse/Attending Physician/Genetic Testing Lab Courier carry role=internal_staff below -- remove their `role` field to show these flows getting skipped instead, for a before/after demo. DF9 (EHR Database->External Insurance Auditor) intentionally stays unreachable either way: External Insurance Auditor is role=external_party, same as genomic's remaining 27 stuck threats.

flows.description: Patient submits daily vitals (heart rate, blood pressure) from a wearable device
Remote Monitoring Platform stores incoming vitals in the EHR database
Nurse directly reviews and annotates a patient's vitals in the EHR database during rounds
Attending Physician calls the patient directly to relay genetic test results and next steps
Genetic Testing Lab Courier physically delivers a sequencing report and uploads results to the store
Clinical Decision Support App pulls genetic test results to screen for risk flags
Clinical Decision Support App sends a flagged high-risk alert to the Attending Physician
Clinical Decision Support App reads recent vitals history from the EHR database
External Insurance Auditor pulls EHR records directly during a billing/coverage audit
